# Slice 1 closed: one file outside the plan, and one command not to run yet

Records 9 (RED), 10 (GREEN) and 11 and 12 (the full suite) close slice 1. Both checks
declare `opus` and the log reads `claude-opus-5`, which is what the route chose. Verified
independently of the implementer's report: record 9 exits 1 on
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'harness.hooks'`, which is the failure the slice's RED
names, and not an assertion about merged content that would have meant the module existed.

## harness/tests/helpers.py is outside slice 1's file list, and was changed anyway

The slice named ten files and this is an eleventh. `make_project` builds every project the
suite tests against, and `doctor.report` now carries a `hook_files` section, so a project
without `harness/hooks.json` and without synced copies fails every existing test that calls
doctor. The two alternatives were both worse: a `sync` that silently does nothing when the
source is absent, or a `drift` that reports nothing, and each bends the module to fit a file
list rather than the other way round.

It is written down here rather than explained at the review because slice 2 builds the guard
that refuses exactly this edit. The refusal would have been correct. The remedy the solution
record names for that case is an amendment through a return to solution; the journal is
append-only, so what stands in for it before the guard exists is this record, and the review
should read the file list of slice 1 as ten files plus this one, with this reason.

## Do not run `python3 harness/run.py sync` before slice 3

`doctor` exits 1 today with ten problems, every one of them from the new `hook_files` section,
each naming the copy and the event. That is the deliberate state, not an unfinished one.

The generated PreToolUse entry calls `python3 harness/run.py hook pre-tool-use --client claude`,
and the dispatcher behind `hook` is slice 3. argparse exits 2 on an unknown command, and exit 2
on PreToolUse is how both assistants spell deny. So a sync run now would refuse every Edit,
Write, MultiEdit and apply_patch in the next session, before slice 2 could write
`harness/guard.py`. This is the first risk record 7 names, arriving exactly where it said it
would, and the mitigation it names is the one in force: sync runs at the end of slice 3.

Two consequences to carry to the next session. CI's harness self-check runs `doctor`, so any
push before slice 3 has run `sync` is a red build, which is why delivery attests a commit after
it rather than before. And the session that does run `sync` should expect the hooks to load at
its next start, which is criterion 2 passing rather than something going wrong.

## Two observations for later, neither in this slice

The source gives PreCompact and SubagentStop to Claude Code alone, because Codex documents
neither event. Criterion 5's Codex session should confirm which of the six `/hooks` lists; if it
takes either after all, `clients` in the source is the one line that changes.

The `statusMessage` key repowise uses on the Codex side is not rendered for harness entries. It
is optional and left out so that drift compares exactly what the renderer writes.
